title: Cannabis and Democracy: Who Are Our Leaders Following? It Ain't  Us!

content_html_sanitized:
In the beautiful state of Idaho, “A 2022 poll commissioned by the Idaho Statesman found that nearly 70% of Idahoans supported legalizing medical marijuana. But even discussions about medical marijuana are shut down in Idaho because of concerns about problems with drugs in liberal cities such as Portland and Seattle.”

 

Of course, cannabis has never been a part of the “problems with drugs” there or anywhere else. And remember, this is about MEDICAL cannabis.

 

An overwhelming share of U.S. adults (88%) say marijuana should be legal for medical or recreational use.

 

And there is even a bill in Congress specifically designed to appeal to Conservatives: Can A Bill Focused on States Rights Get Conservatives to Support Medical Cannabis?

 

Nonetheless, in Washington, a Congressional committee is trying to block cannabis rescheduling. It has no chance of making it through Congress, and Trump would veto it, if it did. But who do these people really represent?

Remember Marijuana Is In Schedule One. Fentanyl Is In Schedule 2. Think About It.

 

Meanwhile, in Europe, there is the same question. In Germany, Survey Reveals Why German Parents Support Cannabis Legalization One Year After Implementation

 

In the most recent German parliamentary elections in Februarythe winning party got less than 29% of the votes, and  the current ruling coalition (CDU/CSU + SPD) received approximately 44.9% of the popular vote, far less than the 60% percent favoring cannabis reform.

 

Their biggest worry is the rise of the far right, which they say is anti democratic. But… the politicians in Berlin seem afraid to follow the people.

 

Meanwhile, the German medical establishment, which kept cannabis illegal for decades, is demanding control over something that they demonstrably know nothing about.

 

One place where there is no mention of cannabis:

Drug-induced deaths – the current situation in Europe (European Drug Report 2025)

 

Germany: New Study Reveals Nearly 150,000 Deaths Due to Alcohol, Tobacco Yearly And Complete Government Failure to Protect People From Avoidable Harm

 

Problematic benzodiazepine use in Germany. It is estimated that 1.5 to 1.9 million persons in Germany are addicted to legal medicine, mainly benzodiazepines, hypnotics and pain killers.

 

Drug overdose deaths

The largest increases in the number of drug-induced deaths in 2023 were reported by Germany, Latvia, Finland, Norway and Türkiye.

Heroin remains involved in large numbers of deaths in some western European countries: over 678 cases in Germany.

Cocaine was involved in 30 % of the overdose deaths in Germany and in 65 % of the overdose deaths in 2023.

The highest numbers of deaths involving non-cocaine stimulants were reported by Germany (490 cases)

Germany reported the largest number of fentanyl-related deaths in Europe (70). Some of these fatalities might be associated with diverted fentanyl medicines rather than illicit fentanyl.

Think of the wasted lives.
